SlashDesk - Third-party notices

Open About > Third-party notices to read the complete license and attribution
texts embedded in this application. No internet connection is required.
The original texts are retained in their original language; only the viewer's
interface is translated. Line endings are normalized to LF / UTF-8 without BOM.
The embedded catalog records document identities, versions, source references
and SHA-256 digests. SlashDesk's own MIT license remains unchanged.

This software is based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

ScreenRecorderLib 6.6.0: Copyright (c) 2017 Sverre Skodje (license text).
The NuGet package metadata also credits Sverre Kristoffer Skodje, copyright 2025.
Tesseract .NET 5.2.0: Copyright 2012-2020 Charles Weld (NuGet metadata).
InteropDotNet: Copyright 2014 Andrey Akinshin (Tesseract acknowledgement).
AvalonEdit 6.3.1.120: AvalonEdit Contributors; NuGet metadata credits
2000-2025 AlphaSierraPapa for the SharpDevelop Team.
See each accompanying upstream text for all authors and license conditions.

The x64 Leptonica export reports GIF 5.2.1, JPEG API 6b / libjpeg-turbo 2.1.4,
PNG 1.6.37, TIFF 4.4.0 and zlib 1.2.13. Static x86 codec strings agree where
observable; x86 binaries are distributed by the upstream package but not loaded
by this x64 application. Native source commits/backports are not attested.
The TIFF binary also contains liblzma diagnostic/codec code; its version is not
available from the supplied package. The XZ Utils 5.2.7 COPYING is supplied as a
supplemental upstream notice, not as an assertion of its exact binary version.
That notice distinguishes the public-domain library from separately licensed
tools/build scripts; no XZ command-line tools are distributed by SlashDesk.

Self-contained builds include the licenses and notices from the exact resolved
.NET runtime packages. Upstream WPF and Windows Forms notices supplement those
packages. Framework-dependent development builds do not redistribute the runtime.
Microsoft Media Foundation, Windows APIs and the external VC++ prerequisites
remain platform components; no separately downloaded codec/encoder executable
or VC++ installer is included by this change.
